newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan to sell state firms shares to citizens.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan to sell state firms shares to citizens.

text.p: Taiwan has given the initial nod to release up to 30 percent of three major state firms, whose net value totals T$1,066 billion, to its 14 million adult citizens, the top economic planning body said on Friday.
"The council plans to release up to 30 percent of shares at three major state firms," an official at the cabinet's Council for Economic Planning and Development said.

Chinese Petroleum Corp, with a net value of T$261 billion, would release its shares as early as in July, followed by T$478 billion Taiwan Power Co. and T$326 billion Chunghwa Telecom, the council official said by telephone.
The official said the share releases would be carried out over a period of time to minimize the impact on the island's capital market.
The 14 million adult citizens of Taiwan could purchase the three state firms' shares through a preferential treatment to prevent concentrated buying by conglomerates.
The adult citizens out of the island's 21 million people would be qualified to buy 300 to 3,000 shares each, another council official said.
The plan was modelled on Singapore Telecommunications Ltd's successful privatisation scheme, he said.

In previous privatisations, local media and analysts had complained that certain private conglomerates had managed to take control of some privatised state firms, calling this a breach of government trust.
Their calls for the government to reform its privatisation procedures resulted in the new high-diffusion scheme.
The state firms share releases could help to alleviate the government's budget deficit, officials have said.
The government, dogged by a shortfall in tax revenue amid a slow economy in the first three quarters, has forecast a fiscal 1996/97 (July/June) deficit of T$87.6 billion.
